title: Two-Stage Seam Composition Run
statement: Let $M_0,M_1,M_2$ be machines with $k$ work tapes over a common alphabet and respective state sets $S_0,S_1,S_2$. Choose states $e_1,e_2\in S_0$ with $e_1\ne e_2$, and entry states $entry_1\in S_1$ and $entry_2\in S_2$. If a run of $M_0$ from configuration $c_0$ reaches $c_1$ after $T_0$ steps and avoids both states $e_1$ and $e_2$ at every earlier time, then the following two conclusions hold: if $c_1$ has state $e_1$, the twice seam-composed machine, run from $c_0$ with its state embedded in the leftmost component, agrees after the handoff and any $t$ further steps with the run of $M_1$ from $c_1$ with state replaced by $entry_1$, embedded in the middle component; if $c_1$ has state $e_2$, it agrees instead with the run of $M_2$ from $c_1$ with state replaced by $entry_2$, embedded in the rightmost component. In each case the claimed agreement holds for every natural number $t$, at time $T_0+1+t$.
hypotheses_covered: $k$ work tapes and a common symbol alphabet and input
The run from $c_0$ reaches $c_1$ at time $T_0$
Before time $T_0$, the run's state is neither $e_1$ nor $e_2$
Each conclusion is conditional on the corresponding endpoint state of $c_1$
The conclusions hold for every natural number $t$
